results.outcome: ICU mortality (mortality at longest follow-up) in the Ptp-guided PEEP group versus control
results.result_location: Table 2 ('Outcome' rows), p. 7; also reported in text, Results, p. 5

1.1.support: A random number was generated by Stata 9.0 (StataCorp, College Station, TX) by an independent statistician, and patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the Ptp group or control group in block sizes of four.
1.1.location: p. 3, Trial Design and Oversight (continues from p. 2)

1.2.support: I looked for any description of allocation concealment (central or remote randomization, or sequentially numbered opaque sealed envelopes) and found none; the report states only that an independent statistician generated the random numbers.
1.2.location: p. 3, Trial Design and Oversight; no concealment statement anywhere in the report

1.3.support: there were baseline differences between the two groups, particularly regarding liver cirrhosis and acute kidney injury. The organ function injury was more severe in the Ptp group.
1.3.location: p. 11, Discussion (limitations); Table 1, p. 6 (acute kidney injury 6 (30) vs 0 (0), p = 0.008; liver cirrhosis 4 (20) vs 0 (0), p = 0.037)

2.3.support: The authors vouch for the completeness and accuracy of the data and for the adherence of the trial to the protocol.

2.7.support: Answered only when 2.6 is No, Probably no or No information; an analysis of all randomized participants was used.

4.1.support: I looked for any indication that ICU mortality was measured inappropriately (an instrument insensitive to plausible effects or of demonstrated poor validity) and found none; ICU mortality is reported as a standard secondary endpoint.

4.2.support: I looked for any indication that death in the ICU was ascertained differently between the groups and found none; the same ICU records were used, with data collection reported as blinded.
4.2.location: p. 3, Trial Design and Oversight; Table 2, p. 7

4.3.support: However, during the entire study period, the data collection and endpoint assessment were blinded, and the statisticians were also blinded during the statistical analysis.

5.1.support: I looked for the trial protocol or registry record containing pre-specified analysis intentions and found none in the report; although the trial is registered (NCT 05629832), no analysis plan is reproduced.
5.1.location: p. 2 and p. 3, Trial Design and Oversight (trial registration); p. 4, Statistical Analysis

5.2.support: I looked for evidence of multiple eligible measurements of ICU mortality (alternative definitions or time points) and found none; a single in-ICU mortality proportion (8/20 vs 7/20) is reported.

5.3.support: I looked for a pre-specified analysis plan defining how ICU mortality was to be analysed and found none; only a single unadjusted between-group comparison (p = 0.744) is reported.

D1.rationale: Allocation used a computer-generated sequence from an independent statistician (1.1 Yes), but concealment until enrolment is not described (1.2 NI), which alone yields Some concerns under the algorithm; additionally the authors acknowledge baseline differences (more acute kidney injury and liver cirrhosis in the Ptp group, 1.3 PY) that they say may have affected outcomes.

D2.rationale: Clinicians delivering the intervention were aware of allocation (2.2 Yes), but no deviations from the intended intervention arising from the trial context are reported (2.3 PN; the authors vouch for protocol adherence), and all 40 randomized participants were analysed (2.6 Yes), so an appropriate analysis estimated the effect of assignment; the algorithm therefore gives Low.

D3.rationale: Outcome data were available for all 40 randomized participants (20 per group, 3.1 Yes); no missing outcome data are described.

D4.rationale: ICU mortality is an objective outcome, measured in the same way in both groups (4.1 N, 4.2 N), and outcome assessment is reported as blinded (4.3 N); knowledge of allocation could not plausibly influence death ascertainment.

D5.rationale: No pre-specified analysis plan or registry entry is available in the report (5.1 NI), which yields Some concerns for selection of the reported result; there is only one eligible measurement of ICU mortality (5.2 N), but the analysis could have been performed in more than one eligible way with no stated intentions (5.3 NI).

overall.rationale: No domain is judged at high risk of bias, but Some concerns in domain 1 (undescribed allocation concealment plus acknowledged baseline imbalance in key prognostic factors, with organ injury more severe in the Ptp group) and in domain 5 (no available pre-specified analysis plan) mean the result of this small single-centre pilot trial cannot be regarded as at low risk of bias.

4.4.support: ICU physicians administered therapies according to the clinical management protocols for hemodynamic resuscitation, sedation, nutritional therapy, anti-infectious treatment, weaning from ventilation, and other related critical care interventions.

5.2.support: I looked for evidence of multiple eligible measurements of the duration of mechanical ventilation (for example ventilator-free days at several time points) and found none; a single median (IQR) of IMV hours is reported.

5.3.support: I looked for a pre-specified analysis plan defining the analysis of IMV duration and found none; only a single unadjusted between-group comparison (p = 0.303) is reported.

D1.rationale: Allocation used a computer-generated sequence from an independent statistician (1.1 Yes), but concealment until enrolment is not described (1.2 NI), which alone yields Some concerns under the algorithm; additionally the authors acknowledge baseline differences (more acute kidney injury and liver cirrhosis in the Ptp group, 1.3 PY).

D2.rationale: Clinicians delivering the intervention were aware of allocation (2.2 Yes), but no deviations from the intended intervention arising from the trial context are reported (2.3 PN) and all 40 randomized participants were analysed (2.6 Yes), so an appropriate analysis estimated the effect of assignment.

D3.rationale: Duration of IMV was reported for all 40 randomized participants (20 per group, 3.1 Yes); no missing outcome data are described.

D4.rationale: The outcome is appropriate and measured with the same approach in both groups (4.1 N, 4.2 N), but duration of IMV is decided by the weaning/extubation decisions of clinicians who knew the allocation (4.3 PY), so assessment could have been influenced (4.4 PY); there is nevertheless no reason to believe that it was, since weaning followed unit protocols and the endpoint was collected by blinded personnel (4.5 PN). The algorithm therefore gives Some concerns rather than Low.

D5.rationale: No pre-specified analysis plan or registry entry is available in the report (5.1 NI), which yields Some concerns; there is a single eligible measurement of IMV duration (5.2 N), but the data could have been analysed in more than one eligible way with no stated intentions (5.3 NI).

overall.rationale: No domain is judged at high risk of bias, but there are Some concerns in domains 1 and 5 for both results plus domain 4 for this outcome, where the duration of ventilation depended on extubation decisions made by clinicians who were aware of the assigned intervention; together these lower confidence in this secondary result from a small single-centre pilot trial.
